answer: Coordinated-Action Pricing. Each agent identity must post a unique per-epoch coordination budget; the protocol charges it per distinct counterparty it signals to within a window. Cost scales superlinearly with the number of fresh identities that share an opal-tagged interaction graph, so a sybil cluster paying itself inflates its own bill. Attackers must either fund many independent budgets or collapse to few identities, and repeated cross-cluster touches leave an ivory trail the pricing uses to raise fees further.
